note: External independent RCWA reference, and an audit of the claims its whitepaper makes about grcwa. Unlike moose_reference.json, this file is not the only way to get the numbers: Ikarus is installable (pip install ikarus-rcwa), so benchmark/run.py and benchmark/conv_run.py compute the 'measured' values live via benchmark/ikarus_suite.py. What is recorded here and cannot be regenerated is the set of values PUBLISHED in the whitepaper, so the live run stays falsifiable against them. Reproduce with: python benchmark/ikarus_whitepaper_check.py

faithful_true_value.claim: the converged reflectance is 10.0% (FMMax, high truncation)
faithful_true_value.evidence: Ikarus normal-vector reaches 0.1002 and this fork's Pol reaches 0.1001

faithful_converges_by_M10.claim: the faithful methods reach the true value by M ~ 10
faithful_converges_by_M10.evidence: Ikarus NV is at 0.1003 by q = 15 (M = 7) and flat thereafter

direct_rule_is_O_1_over_M.claim: the direct rule crawls in from above and is still a quarter too high at M = 30
direct_rule_is_O_1_over_M.evidence: fork Laurent: 0.1631 (q=25), 0.1367 (q=41), 0.1143 (q=101), 0.1071 (q=201) -- monotone from above, still 7% high at 201 orders

energy_balance_is_not_convergence.claim: R+T = 1 to machine precision throughout that wrong convergence

grcwa_is_a_direct_rule_solver.claim: grcwa uses the direct rule and so misses the faithful value by 60-75%
grcwa_is_a_direct_rule_solver.verdict: true of upstream grcwa, NOT of this fork
grcwa_is_a_direct_rule_solver.evidence: upstream is Laurent-only (its Pol did not converge for TM; see tests/test_pol_correctness.py). This fork's FIXED Pol converges to 0.1001, i.e. onto the faithful value, and on the curved 2D case D2 it tracks Ikarus's normal-vector result (0.9286 vs 0.9265) rather than its Li result (0.8732).

grcwa_row_audit.finding: Table 1's grcwa value is the Laurent rule at ~23 x-orders, not at 400.
grcwa_row_audit.cause: The paper's harness (ikarus/tests/validation/grcwa_reference.py: grating_RT) drives this 1D grating through a SQUARE 2D lattice, L1=[1,0] and L2=[0,1], with a 2D circular truncation. A y-invariant layer couples only to Gy=0, so of a nominal nG=400 (385 actually retained) just 23 orders lie on Gy=0 and do any work.
grcwa_row_audit.conclusion: The physics claim stands -- Laurent really is O(1/M) and really is ~75% high at that truncation. Only the framing overstates it: 'still badly off even at 400 orders' is off at 23 effective orders. Given a native 1D truncation of 385 orders the same code gives 0.1037.

performance.note: min-of-3 wall time per solve at nG = 121, from benchmark/results.csv on one machine -- indicative only, not a controlled comparison.
performance.comment: Ikarus's NumPy core costs roughly 2-5x grcwa per solve at matched order count; on the high-contrast TM cases that is bought back many times over, since it needs ~15 orders where Laurent needs far more than 200.
